name: Extreme heat
summary: Brazil's heat peaked near 40°C in mid-November without meeting the heatwave definition; no deadly heatwave found
state: Parts of Brazil's Central-West, North and Northeast reached about 40°C in mid-November, with Porto Murtinho at 39.8°C on 13 Nov, but the spell did not meet the national met institute's heatwave definition and no deaths were reported (Latin Times, 16 Nov). Queensland's severe heatwave warning ran only to 19 Nov (The Watchers). Searches on 22 Nov found no heatwave warning across a major region, no national record and no deadly heatwave, so Normal holds.
for_you: Southern-hemisphere summer heat is building. People travelling to Brazil, southern Africa or northern Australia should follow local met service warnings; the elderly, young children and outdoor workers are most exposed.
rubric_hit: No heatwave warnings across a major region or national records = Normal

sources.title: Latin Times — Brazil heat surge: temperatures near 40°C in November

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
